## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

```{r}
#guardamos
dir.create("data/processed", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
st_write(PERGAMINO,   "data/processed/pergamino_area.gpkg",    delete_dsn = TRUE)
st_write(calles_osm,  "data/processed/calles_osm_raw.gpkg",    delete_dsn = TRUE)
st_write(calles_line, "data/processed/calles_line.gpkg",       delete_dsn = TRUE)

dir.create("data/raw", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("data/processed", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

saveRDS(calles_osm, "data/raw/calles_osm.rds")
saveRDS(calles_per, "data/processed/calles_per.rds")
saveRDS(calles_line, "data/processed/calles_line.rds")
saveRDS(calles_linered, "data/processed/calles_linered.rds")
saveRDS(calle_aux, "data/processed/calle_aux.rds")
saveRDS(calles_lineimp, "data/processed/calles_lineimp.rds")
saveRDS(lineint, "data/processed/lineint.rds")
saveRDS(perga_net, file = "red_pergamino_preprocesada.rds")
saveRDS(perga_net2, file = "red_pergamino_procesada.rds")
saveRDS(perganet_aux, file = "data/processed/perganet_aux.rds")
saveRDS(perganet_clean, file = "data/processed/perganet_clean.rds")
saveRDS(resumen_perga, file = "data/processed/resumen_perga.rds")
saveRDS(comp_4_net, file = "data/processed/comp_4_net.rds")

perga_net2 <- readRDS(perga_net2, file = "red_pergamino_procesada.rds")
```

```{r}

factpal <- colorFactor(topo.colors(length(unique(calles_linered$highway))),
                       calles_linered$highway)
calles_linered |>
  st_transform(5347) |>
  filter(is.na(oneway)) |>
  leaflet() |>
  addTiles() |>
  addPolylines(color = ~factpal(highway),
               popup = ~ paste0("Tipo: ", highway, "<br>Mano única: ", oneway ) ) |>
  addLegend(pal = factpal, values = ~highway, title = "Tipo de camino")

rm(factpal)
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(calles_linered) +
  # Evaluamos is.na() directamente dentro de aes()
  geom_sf(aes(color = is.na(maxspeed)), linewidth = 0.5) +
  # Personalizamos los colores y las etiquetas de la leyenda al vuelo
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("TRUE" = "gray80", "FALSE" = "firebrick"),
    labels = c("TRUE" = "Sin velocidad (NA)", "FALSE" = "Con velocidad")
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(color = "Estado")
```

```{r}


ggplot(calles_per) +
  # Mapeamos el color directamente a la columna highway
  geom_sf(aes(color = highway), linewidth = 0.5) +
  
  # Usamos una paleta de colores cualitativa linda (como viridis plasma o colorbrewer)
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") +

  labs(
    title = "Red vial de Pergamino por tipo de vía",
    subtitle = "Clasificación según OpenStreetMap (highway)",
    color = "Tipo de vía"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
```

```{r}
library(tibble)
library(sfnetworks)
library(igraph)
library(dplyr)

resumen_perga <- tibble(
  red = "Pergamino (Componente Principal)",
  nodos = igraph::gorder(perganet_clean),
  ejes = igraph::gsize(perganet_clean),
  longitud_km = perganet_clean |> 
    activate("edges") |> 
    as_tibble() |> 
    pull(edge_length()) |> 
    sum(na.rm = TRUE) |> 
    units::set_units("m") |> 
    units::set_units("km") |> 
    as.numeric() |> 
    round(2),
  grado_medio = mean(igraph::degree(perganet_clean)) |> round(2),
  densidad = igraph::edge_density(perganet_clean) |> round(6)
)
```

```{r}


resumen_perga <- tibble(
  red = "Pergamino (Componente Principal)",
  nodos = igraph::gorder(perganet_clean),
  ejes = igraph::gsize(perganet_clean),
  
  # Corrección para extraer la longitud total sin el error de edge_length()
  longitud_km = perganet_clean |> 
    activate("edges") |> 
    as_tibble() |> 
    mutate(len = st_length(geometry)) |> 
    pull(len) |> 
    sum(na.rm = TRUE) |> 
    units::set_units("m") |> 
    units::set_units("km") |> 
    as.numeric() |> 
    round(2),
  
  grado_medio = mean(igraph::degree(perganet_clean)) |> round(2),
  densidad = igraph::edge_density(perganet_clean) |> round(6)
)
```

```{r}
library(sfnetworks)
library(dplyr)

perganet_clean |> 
  activate("edges") |> 
  as_tibble() |> 
  head()
```

```{r}


ggplot() +
  # Dibujamos las aristas coloreadas según tu campo imputado maxspeed_imp
  geom_sf(
    data = st_as_sf(perganet_clean, "edges"), 
    aes(color = as.factor(maxspeed_imp)), 
    linewidth = 0.6, 
    alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  
  # Paleta de colores para las distintas categorías de velocidad
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Velocidad Máxima\nImputada (km/h)",
    values = c(
      "30" = "gray70",      # Calles locales
      "40" = "skyblue",     # Colectoras secundarias
      "60" = "orange",      # Avenidas
      "80" = "firebrick",   # Rutas o arterias rápidas
      "110" = "darkviolet"  # Autopistas / Circunvalación
    ),
    na.value = "grey85"     # Color de respaldo para tramos sin valor
  ) +
  
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12)
  ) +
  labs(title = "Jerarquía Vial de Pergamino por Velocidad Imputada")
```

```{r}


ggplot() +
  # Dibujamos las aristas coloreadas según maxspeed_imp como factor
  geom_sf(
    data = st_as_sf(perganet_clean, "edges"), 
    aes(color = as.factor(maxspeed_imp)), 
    linewidth = 0.6, 
    alpha = 0.85
  ) +
  
  # Opción A: Usando paleta Viridis discreta (excelente contraste visual)
  scale_color_viridis_d(
    name = "Velocidad\n(km/h)",
    option = "viridis", # Probá también con "viridis", "inferno", "cividis" o "magma"
    na.value = "grey80"
  ) +
  
  # O P C I Ó N  B (Comentada): Si preferís una paleta tipo ColorBrewer (ej: "YlOrRd")
  # scale_color_brewer(
  #   name = "Velocidad\n(km/h)",
  #   palette = "YlOrRd", # Amarillo-Naranja-Rojo (ideal para velocidad)
  #   na.value = "grey80"
  # ) +
  
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA) 
  ) +
  labs(title = "Jerarquía Vial de Pergamino")

ggsave(
  filename = "Pergamino_velocidades.png", 
  width = 8,       # Ancho en pulgadas
  height = 6,      # Alto en pulgadas
  dpi = 300        # Resolución (300 dpi es estándar de calidad para impresión/papers)
)
```
